content.comment_body: Hello, I have encountered a similar issue where I want to prevent the C1 to C4 keys on the [product_name] operator display from scrolling through screens during RUN mode, unless it is required by the control program. You previously recommended setting the system to operator mode to disable the C1 to C4 keys unless activated by the program logic. I have checked the settings for [product_name] and the operator panel but I could not find how to implement this. Could you please provide guidance?

Unfortunately, it is not possible to deactivate the cursor keys (C1 to C4) on either the base module or the operator display panel in order to stop scrolling between active message screens while in RUN mode. Switching to operator mode only restricts certain operations, such as limiting access to some menu items, but it does not fully deactivate these keys.

analysis.insight_summary: Users want to modify the functionality of the C1 to C4 keys on the operator display, aiming to restrict screen navigation in RUN mode unless specifically initiated by the program. However, it appears that disabling these keys is not supported, which restricts user customization and control over hardware interactions.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to be able to disable or customize the response of the C1 to C4 keys on the operator display in RUN mode so they only work when explicitly programmed.
